value.rationale: The bielliptic Picard family is a canonical Shimura/Prym family, rather than an arbitrary slice. A uniform all-prime classification of its nonordinary divisor as m genuinely double points, with exact p-rank one and a-number two there and no rank-two/zero cases, is a natural geometric invariant; squarefreeness yields a nontrivial transversality-with-multiplicity statement of use for specialization and modular arithmetic. It is not merely finite-field enumeration or a trivial general Hasse-Witt algorithm.
